metadata.title: Cybersecurity pipelines hit 11-quarter high as buyers consolidate vendors

content.text:
Jefferies survey points to faster market growth in 2027, with cloud security and broader platforms emerging as priorities.
Cybersecurity sales pipelines strengthened in the third quarter, with no surveyed reseller reporting a decline for the first time in 11 quarters, Jefferies found.
The investment bank's survey of 25 value-added resellers estimated average pipeline growth at 5.6%, up from 3.9% in the second quarter.
76% of respondents reported improving pipelines over the previous three months, 24% saw no change, and 0% reported a decline.
Resellers raised their expected cybersecurity market growth for the calendar year 2026 to 10.2%, from 9.6% in July, and forecast growth accelerating to 12.2% in 2027.
The findings point to strengthening demand as customers increasingly consolidate security spending around fewer suppliers and integrated technology platforms.
Survey respondents described buyers moving away from stand-alone security tools towards integrated suites covering network security, cloud protection, identity and data governance.
Jefferies identified Cloudflare, the internet infrastructure and security company, Palo Alto Networks Inc (NASDAQ:PANW, XETRA:5AP), the cybersecurity platform provider, and CrowdStrike Holdings Inc (NASDAQ:CRWD), the endpoint security specialist, as leading performers in reseller feedback.
The three companies recorded net performance scores of 58%, 56% and 43%, respectively, measuring the proportion of respondents reporting results above plan minus those reporting results below plan.
Cloud security emerged as the fastest-growing expected category over the next 12 months and the leading area for investment aimed at securing generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
AI-related security spending is also beginning to feed through, with 88% of respondents reporting that customer budgets had changed or were expected to change following security concerns associated with Mythos.
44% said the spending benefit began in the third quarter, while another 24% expected it to emerge during the final three months of 2026.
Microsoft strengthened its perceived lead in agentic identity security, with 60% of respondents identifying it as well positioned, while CyberArk/Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike each received 48%.
Higher memory prices may also be accelerating purchases of firewall appliances, with an average of 48% of respondents reporting some pull-forward in spending across Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet and Check Point.
The report cautioned that the findings reflect a limited sample of 25 resellers surveyed in early October and do not quantify the financial impact of AI-related budget increases.
